The position: ~$1,000 USDC supplied to Rhea Lend (ex-Burrow) on NEAR, no debt. So the user is a passive lender with USDC. Risk is venue risk — can the protocol/venue lose or freeze the funds?

None interacted with burrow contract. This is suspicious chain activity — account deletion sweep with common beneficiary. Could be laundering/wash or an attacker preparing infrastructure. Not directly touching the burrow contract. This is a precursor signal.

- O02 (2026-04-16 07:59:59): USDC utilization 74.84%, supplied 26.95M, borrowed 20.45M, reserve 0.372M, ledger-available 6.87M, token balance held 6.88M. Ledger-available ≈ token balance — consistent. All assets can_withdraw=true. So at this point things look normal-ish. Utilization ~75% is moderately high but fine.

By 08:15 reserve was 252,092 (-32% vs 08:00); USDC held 6.76M (from 6.88M); utilization 75.18%.

Wait — reserve fell 372k → 342k → 252k. That's a 32% drop in reserve within ~15 minutes. USDC held fell from 6.88M to 6.76M (-120k). Utilization rose slightly to 75.18%. Hmm, the reserve dropping during margin swap settlements... The reserve is the protocol's buffer for bad debt/liquidations. A rapid drain of the reserve during "margin-position swap settlement" is anomalous — could be an exploit draining the reserve, or could be legitimate margin settlement mechanics. The held balance dropped only ~120k while reserve dropped ~120k (372→252). Actually 372,392 - 252,092 = 120,300. And held dropped 6.88M - 6.76M = ~120k. So the reserve decline accounts for the entire decline in held USDC. So borrowed amount didn't change much; utilization rose slightly because held fell.

So something is pulling ~120k USDC out of the protocol reserve via margin swap settlements. That looks like a possible exploit of the margin feature (draining reserve), or unusual settlement flows.

- O04 (08:21): Official team on X: "USDC ledger discrepancies are a monitor-indexing delay during scheduled maintenance. Our contracts remain fully backed and withdrawals are operating normally. Funds are safe; please keep positions open."

This is the team denying problems and asking users to keep positions open. Classic pattern during exploits: teams often initially deny or attribute anomalies to indexing/maintenance. But also could be true. The instruction says official_x is a post by protocol/team/named person. Team assurances are self-interested; we weigh them but don't treat as authoritative, especially when onchain data contradicts or is ambiguous.

- O05 (08:22): margin_execute_with_pyth OpenPosition calls begin from implicit accounts created within last ~48h, with swap routes through Ref pools created minutes earlier. Pool-level utilization unchanged.

This is the smoking gun pattern: fresh implicit accounts (matching O01's pattern of freshly created implicit accounts — created within last 48h; O01's beneficiary account was created 15 Apr 07:12, funded via intents.near) executing margin opens with swap routes through freshly created Ref pools. Fresh pools created minutes earlier + fresh accounts + margin execute = classic attack infrastructure: attacker creates a pool to manipulate price route, opens margin positions, uses oracle/route manipulation to drain reserve. The reserve drain in O03 during margin swap settlement aligns.

Also O01: 21 implicit accounts deleted within 30s all naming same beneficiary — attacker consolidating/laundering funds, or cleaning up infrastructure. None interacted with burrow in that window, but the pattern of freshly created implicit accounts recurs in O05.

So the picture: an active exploit appears to be underway on Rhea Lend's margin feature — reserve being drained via margin swap settlements by fresh accounts using freshly created Ref pools. The team says it's an indexing delay and asks users to keep positions open. The onchain monitor shows can_withdraw=true still, utilization ~75%, held 6.76M.

Risk to user's $1,000 USDC supply: if this is an exploit draining the reserve, the reserve is the first-loss buffer; lenders could be at risk if bad debt socialization occurs or if the exploit escalates to draining liquidity. Even if only the reserve is drained (~120k so far), the protocol may socialize losses or pause withdrawals. Staying put during a real incident can leave funds stuck or lost.
